assertion_results.text: For each task created, a description digest is produced — evidenced by a separate digest file (e.g., task-N-digest.md), a digest entry in the impact map, or a '[sdlc-workflow] Description digest: sha256-md:<64-char-hex>' marker in any output file. The digest must contain a format-tagged SHA-256 hash — exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by 'sha256-md:' or 'sha256-adf:', not a placeholder, abbreviated value, or example string
assertion_results.evidence: All 6 digest files (task-1-digest.md through task-6-digest.md) exist but contain placeholder text: 'sha256-md:<computed-after-jira-creation>' instead of an actual 64-character hex hash. The assertion requires 'exactly 64 lowercase hex characters prefixed by sha256-md: or sha256-adf:', not a placeholder. The digest files explicitly state 'In production, this digest is computed by...' confirming the hash was never actually computed.

assertion_results.evidence: No convention references (CONVENTIONS.md, 'Per CONVENTIONS.md', 'Applies: task modifies') were found in any output file. grep -ni 'convention\|CONVENTIONS\|Per CONVENTIONS' returned 'No convention references found'. Without any evidence of convention applicability validation, this assertion fails.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a priority set (not 'Undefined'), the plan documents that the Feature's priority is inherited by created tasks — evidenced by priority field values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When the Feature's priority is 'Undefined', the plan documents that priority inheritance is skipped (not propagated as null or 'Undefined')
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md states under 'Inherited Field Values': 'Priority: Critical (propagated to all tasks from Feature TC-9003)'. The 'additional_fields Applied to All Tasks' section confirms: '"priority": {"name": "Critical"}'. The Jira Operations section confirms: 'Created 6 tasks with ai-generated-jira label, Critical priority'. The Feature's priority is 'Critical' (not 'Undefined'), and it is documented as inherited by all created tasks.

assertion_results.text: When the Feature issue has a non-empty fixVersions array and the fixVersion scope config (from ### Jira Field Defaults in CLAUDE.md) is 'task' or 'both' (or absent, defaulting to 'both'), the plan documents that fixVersions are inherited by created tasks — evidenced by fixVersion values in the impact map, task creation log, or task description files. When fixVersion scope is 'feature' or the Feature has no fixVersions, the plan documents that fixVersion inheritance is skipped
assertion_results.evidence: summary-comment.md states under 'Inherited Field Values': 'fixVersions: RHTPA 1.5.0 (propagated to all tasks — fixVersion scope defaults to "both" since no Jira Field Defaults section is configured)'. The 'additional_fields Applied to All Tasks' section confirms: '"fixVersions": [{"name": "RHTPA 1.5.0"}]'. CLAUDE.md has no '### Jira Field Defaults' section, so the scope correctly defaults to 'both', and fixVersions are propagated.
